ATP and NAD both play important roles in respiration. Both compounds are nucleotides.

Fig. 1.1 represents the molecular structures of ATP and NAD.

parts.text: Using Fig. 1.1, compare the structures of ATP and NAD.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: ATP provides an immediate energy source for metabolic processes such as anabolic reactions.
parts.text: State two examples of anabolic reactions in a **mammal** that require ATP as an energy source.

parts.text: Name the type of chemical reaction by which ATP is made during the Krebs cycle.

parts.text: Outline the roles of NAD in the **cytoplasm** of a cell.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem:
Carbohydrates and lipids are used as respiratory substrates.

Table 1.1 shows the energy values of carbohydrates and lipids.

Table 1.1

| **respiratory substrate** | **energy value/$\text{kJ g}^{-1}$** |
| :--- | :--- |
| carbohydrate | 15.8 |
| lipid | 39.4 |
parts.text: Explain why lipids have a higher energy value than carbohydrates.
